author: Blyth, 1842
habitat: 논, 밭, 개울가 풀숲, 모래밭, 초습지
summary: 우리나라에서는 해마다 10건 미만으로 기록되는 길잃은새로, 논, 밭, 개울가 풀숲, 모래밭, 초습지 등에 찾아온다. 번식기가 아닐 때는 무리 지어 지낸다. 곤충, 지렁이, 파충류, 물고기 등을 먹고, 풀숲이나 잔디, 자갈밭의 오목한 곳에 둥지를 지어 알 3~4개를 27~30일 동안 품는다. 시베리아 남부, 몽골, 중국, 일본에 분포한다.

points.en: yellow bill with a black tip
black line between brown upperparts and white underparts

art.subject: Grey-headed Lapwing (Vanellus cinereus), adult in breeding plumage, as seen in Korean rice fields in spring (March–April): head, neck and upper breast plain ash-grey; a broad blackish band across the lower breast; back, scapulars and wing coverts plain light brown; primaries black; belly, flanks and undertail white; rump white; tail white with a broad black subterminal band; bill yellow with a black tip; a small yellow wattle in front of the eye; iris red; legs long, yellow.
art.pose: standing in a rice field, scanning the ground
art.scene: Korean rice paddies and grassy stream banks in spring (March–April), stubble and shallow water in flat light; no people, buildings or text
views: adult breeding, side view standing in a rice field: ash-grey head, neck and breast, blackish band separating the grey breast from the white belly, plain brown back and wings, black-tipped yellow bill, small yellow loral wattle, red eye, long dull yellow legs

adult, in flight seen from above, head, body and tail in line: brown back and coverts, broad white panel across the secondaries, black primaries, white rump and white tail with a black band near the tip
adult, head detail in profile: grey head without a crest, yellow bill with a black tip, small yellow wattle in front of the red eye
art.build: Large, long-legged lapwing, 36cm, a little longer than a feral pigeon and noticeably larger than Northern Lapwing; upright, with a rather long neck. Rounded head with no crest. Bill straight, plover-like, shorter than the head. Legs long, yellow, with much bare tibia; the feet project beyond the tail in flight. At rest the wingtips reach about the tail tip. In flight the broad, rounded wings show three blocks: brown inner coverts, an all-white panel across the secondaries and greater coverts, and black primaries; white rump and white tail with a black subterminal band.
avoid: Do not add a crest or an iridescent green back; those belong to Northern Lapwing (Vanellus vanellus).
Do not paint the tail brown; it is white with a broad black band near the tip.
Do not paint a red bill or a large red facial wattle (Red-wattled Lapwing); the bill is yellow with a black tip and the wattle small and yellow.
Do not run the black line along the flanks; it is a band across the lower breast below the grey.
